# The Role of Amazon New Act: Automation Web with AI Agents at AWS

The video features Amazon Nova Act, the AWS service to create and manage fleets of AI agents that automate interface flows in the browser. It explains why traditional scripts break, the development cycle, human intervention with approval or assumption of control and the price per hour of agent, which does not count the human waiting time.

Video by Maurício Yokoyama Issei, published on October 18, 2026 (7 min 41 s).
Watch: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=iCVD5IVVR2g

_The video and the transcript are in Portuguese. The minutes between brackets, such as [04:12], point to the excerpt of the video._

## Web automation that does not break

The video deals with web interface automation, an area that usually gives the engineering teams a headache. The focus is the role of Amazon Nova Act in the passage of rigid navigation rules to something more adaptable [00:00].

The central question is how to make web automation resilient. The problem was never writing the script, but keeping it working: any change in the page broke everything, like a house of cards at a table [00:21].

The script involves traditional automation, the role of the New Act, the development journey, human intervention and applications and costs [00:41].

## The pains of traditional automation

Traditional scripts are fragile. Layouts change all the time: a button moves a pixel, a class changes its name, and the whole test fails [01:04].

This consumes the energy of the teams, weighs on the QA tests and forces them to hunt documentation to keep everything in order. The model does not scale with today's dynamic web [01:25].

## What is the New Act

Amazon Nova Act is an AWS service for those who develop and manage fleets of trusted AI agents, who automate interface flows [01:46].

The keyword is fleet: it is not about automating one click, but orchestrating many agents and climbing the operation to the corporate level [01:46].

According to the video, the engine is Amazon Nova 2 Lite, a custom template to browse the web and call APIs quickly and cheaply. It understands the context of an interface, without fixed rules telling where to click [02:07].

According to the video, AWS reports reliability above 90% on a large scale, which transforms a fragile process into a production-ready process [02:28].

## The development journey

AWS drew a four-step path [03:10]:

1. Test ideas on the Playground web [03:10].
2. Develop locally, in the usual environment [03:10].
3. Deploy in the AWS cloud [03:10].
4. Review executions in the service panel [03:10].

In the SDK in Python, natural language blends with code. In an authentication decorator, for example, you can combine rigid logic such as injecting an access token with simple text instructions [03:31].

According to the video, IDE extensions with AI, for Kiro, VS Code and Cursor, transform a request into natural language into ready Python code [03:52].

For observability, the console brings complete tracking of executions. According to the video, you can watch live the browser operated by AI, thanks to AgentCore, in addition to accessing logs on S3 and screenshots [04:33].

## The human touch

Integration with people (human-in-the-loop) has two standards [04:55]:

- Human approval: someone reviews and approves the actions proposed by the agent before a critical execution [04:55].
- Interface control assumption: the flow pauses, a person takes over the browser, solves a CAPTCHA or types a sensitive password and returns control to the agent [05:17].

Business detail: the time when the system expects a human response does not enter the account. It is like a meter that stops, and so the security breaks do not generate idle cost [05:17].

## Applications and costs

One use case is retail price intelligence. Monitoring the competition has always been difficult because stores change the layout and break the trackers; the New Act handles these changes [05:59].

Other cases are web quality tests, data extraction from legacy systems and purchasing flows with many steps [05:59].

The price released is US$ 4.75 per hour of agent, counting only active hours [06:21]. Compared to hours spent fixing broken scripts, the video considers competitive value [06:42].

The New Act is also part of the Strands Agents Framework. Visual automation becomes a skill among others, in an ecosystem of agents that solve complex flows [06:42].

## End of broken script

The final reflection: reliable and resilient agents will change today's operational bottlenecks. No need to fix a script because someone changed the color of a button is, according to the video, the beginning of a new phase of web automation [07:03].

## Frequently Asked Questions

### How much does Amazon Nova Act cost?

$4.75 an hour, counting only active time. The waiting for a human response is not charged [06:21].

### How does the New Act deal with CAPTCHA and login?

By the assumption of control: the flow pauses, a person solves the step in the browser and returns the control to the agent [05:17].

## About the video

In this video, we explore **The Role of Amazon New Act**, the AWS service developed to create, deploy and manage fleets of AI agents focused on automation of user interface flows (IU) in the browser. 

Learn how the New Act combines the flexibility of instructions in natural language with Python code to automate repetitive and complex tasks, such as input and data extraction, QA testing and checkout flows.

📌 **What you will check in this video:**
- **What is Amazon New Act:** A vertically integrated solution for browser automation with high reliability and scale execution.
- **Architecture and Reliability:** Model training in simulated environments (*web gyms*) to ensure high completion rates even on dynamic websites.
- **Human-in-the-Loop (HITL):** How Service Allows Human Intervention in Real Time (*UI takeover*) or asynchronous approval to solve CAPTCHAs and login steps.
- **Advanced Integrations:** Connection with external APIs, MCP protocol support and native integration with the framework *Strands Agents* and *Amazon Bedrock AgentCore*.
- **Prices and Costs in AWS:** Understand the real-time execution-based pricing model (**$4.75 an hour as an agent**), free of charge in the waiting time for human interventions.

🔗 **Useful Resources and Links:**
- Official Amazon Documentation New Act: https://docs.aws.amazon.com/pt_br/nova-act/
- Official AWS Price Table : https://aws.amazon.com/pt/nova/pricing/
